sentences.text: Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.
3. Learned Counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds of petition submits that the petitioner is in custody from 11.11.2023.
Though initially FIR was also registered for the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC, in the charge sheet, the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC is deleted.
The NC: 2024:KHC:32738 maximum punishment for the alleged offences is imprisonment for a period of three years.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
4. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the bail petition and prays to dismiss the petition.

5. The material on record goes to show that on the basis of the first information dated 10.11.2023 submitted by the victim, Chamarajanagar East Police Station had initially registered FIR in Crime No.204/2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 417, 323, 354, 376 & 506 & 511 of IPC.
Petitioner was arrested in the said case and remanded to the judicial custody on 11.11.2023.
After completion of investigation, the police have now filed charge sheet against the petitioner for offences punishable under Sections 417, 323, 354(A), 354(B) and 506 of IPC IPC.
After charge sheet, offence punishable under Sections 376 and 511 of IPC have been deleted in the present case.

The maximum punishment for the charge sheeted offences is imprisonment for a period of seven NC:
2024:KHC:32738 years.
Petitioner is in custody ever since 11.11.2023.
He has no criminal antecedents.
Considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter, I am of the opinion that petitioner's request for grant of regular bail is required to be answered in the affirmative.
